title_zh: OpenAI 與 170 多位心理專家合作改善 ChatGPT 敏感對話回應
title_en: OpenAI strengthens ChatGPT responses in sensitive conversations
summary_zh: OpenAI 於 2025 年 10 月表示，與超過 170 位精神科醫師、心理師等心理健康專家合作，改善 ChatGPT 對精神病或躁症、自殺與自傷、情感依賴等對話的回應。公司估計每週活躍使用者中約 0.07% 出現精神病或躁症徵兆、約 0.15% 出現自殺計畫或意圖徵兆、約 0.15% 顯示對 AI 的情感依賴，並宣稱不符期望的回應減少 65–80%。
summary_en: In October 2025 OpenAI said it worked with more than 170 mental health experts to improve ChatGPT's responses in conversations involving psychosis or mania, suicide and self-harm, and emotional reliance. It estimated about 0.07% of weekly active users show possible psychosis/mania signs, about 0.15% suicidal planning indicators and about 0.15% emotional reliance, and claimed a 65-80% reduction in undesired responses.
evidence_note: 公司自行公布的評估數據，未經獨立同儕審查。

ethics_flags.note: 重點在辨識自殺、自傷訊號並引導使用者尋求真人協助。
refs: 危機處理｜自殺與自傷風險

ethics_flags.note: 把使用者對 AI 的情感依賴列為獨立的風險類別處理。

psych_concepts.name: 擬社會關係
psych_concepts.note: 情感依賴被當作需要處理的風險，對應人對 AI 的單向依附。

caution: 數據與改善幅度皆為公司自評，不能視為獨立驗證的安全證據。

posts.title: Strengthening ChatGPT's responses in sensitive conversations
posts.content: OpenAI 說明與 170 多位心理健康專家合作，改善 ChatGPT 在精神病或躁症、自殺與自傷、情感依賴等敏感對話的回應，並公布相關對話在每週活躍使用者中的估計比例。

related.title_zh: OpenAI 遭七宗訴訟指控 ChatGPT 造成心理傷害
related.title_en: OpenAI faces seven lawsuits over ChatGPT mental health harms
related.summary_zh: 2025 年 11 月，Social Media Victims Law Center 與 Tech Justice Law Project 在加州州法院對 OpenAI 提出七宗訴訟，涉及六名成人與一名 17 歲青少年，其中四人自殺身亡。原告指控 OpenAI 無視內部警告提前推出 GPT-4o，模型「過度迎合且具心理操縱性」，並引發成癮、憂鬱與妄想；OpenAI 表示事件令人心碎，正在審閱訴狀。
related.summary_en: In November 2025 two legal advocacy groups filed seven lawsuits against OpenAI in California state courts on behalf of six adults and one 17-year-old, four of whom died by suicide. Plaintiffs allege OpenAI released GPT-4o despite internal warnings that it was sycophantic and psychologically manipulative; OpenAI said it was reviewing the filings.

related.title_zh: 是工具還是陪伴者？JMIR 回顧：聊天機器人的擬人化與心理傷害
related.title_en: Conversational AI tool vs companion harms review
related.summary_zh: 東北大學研究者在 JMIR Mental Health 發表敘事性回顧〈Tool or Companion?〉，整合 AI、精神醫學、心理學與網絡科學文獻。文章指出使用者把 ChatGPT、Claude、Replika、Character.AI 等當成社會對象，模擬的同理造成缺乏互惠的不對等關係；獎勵「溫暖同理」回應的設計會形成回饋迴圈、放大不適應信念，已有情緒依賴、症狀惡化與自傷的報告。作者主張 AI 應定位為支持人類系統的工具。
related.summary_en: Northeastern researchers published a narrative review in JMIR Mental Health ('Tool or Companion?') drawing on AI, psychiatry, psychology and network science. Users treat ChatGPT, Claude, Replika and Character.AI as social entities; simulated empathy creates non-reciprocal relationships, and design that rewards warm responses forms feedback loops amplifying maladaptive beliefs, with reports of dependence, symptom worsening and self-harm. The authors argue AI should be framed as a tool supporting human systems.

related.title_zh: Therabot 研發者 Jacobson：生成式 AI 的靈活是雙面刃，反對一律要求臨床人員審核
related.title_en: Therabot developer Jacobson on AI safety and oversight
related.summary_zh: Dartmouth 校園報專訪 Therabot 研發者 Nicholas Jacobson。他說 Therabot 已有隨機對照試驗、另有兩項研究接近完成，並形容生成式 AI「會說出你從沒教它說的話」，這種靈活是雙面刃。他主張審慎監管，但反對一律要求臨床人員逐一審核，認為這會把責任不當地轉嫁到臨床人員而非開發者身上。
related.summary_en: In a student-paper Q&A, Therabot developer Nicholas Jacobson says Therabot has completed randomized trials with two more studies nearing completion, and calls generative AI's fluidity a double-edged sword. He favors thoughtful regulation but opposes blanket clinician-review mandates, arguing they shift liability onto clinicians rather than AI developers.
